audit.why: FAVOURED at 4/10 matches 51.58% over 952 games and the shape of the matchup: Irelia owns levels 1-11, Kassadin owns the late game.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike language never used Riftwalk's real cooldown, which is the entire scaling story: 5s at rank 1, 3.5s at rank 2, 2s at rank 3.
audit.why: Kassadin's power curve IS the Riftwalk rank. Naming the numbers makes 'punish him early' concrete.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, phases[6].why and report[5].t now carry 5s/2s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions were absent: Null Sphere is an interruptible cast that Flawless Duet cancels; its shield absorbs MAGIC damage only, so Irelia's on-hit build walks through it; Nether Blade is a 7s auto-attack reset whose wind-up is the burst tell.
audit.why: All three change how you time the all-in, and all three were unstated on the page.
audit.corrected: Added to dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.carry.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content layer calls Null Sphere a silence (whys[0], wants.foe[1], early). Riot's description gives it damage, channel interruption and a magic shield — no silence.
audit.why: The kit file is authority on ability text; advising the reader to play around a silence that no longer exists is a live error.
audit.corrected: Flagged in notes; whys[0] is a content-layer chart string left alone rather than half-fixed, but the full-layer fields now describe the real effect.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].side read 'Skill' while content win[6] read 'Kassadin' — the page answered 'who wins at 2+ items' two different ways.
audit.why: Packet levelChart row 7 is Kassadin and the prose agrees; the full layer was the stale one.
audit.corrected: phases[6].side, .rating and .why moved to Kassadin together; win[6] already reads Kassadin so no content edit is needed.

edits.before: Late Irelia surfs the fight: Q-reset through their line, stun the carry pair, and shred whoever peels.
edits.after: Riftwalk drops to 2s at rank 3 — he blinks in, bursts, and hops out before your 6s Bladesurge can follow.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to a ranked-up Riftwalk, where 2s blinks let him burst you and leave before you re-stack.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Check it before every step-up. - W Defiant Dance is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and only 2s at rank 3, so his exit becomes real the moment he ranks it. - Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1 and needs spell charges before it fires. - Null Sphere is 9s: bait the shield out, then commit.

edits.before: First item onward, the wave is a weapon: crash it into all-ins, R the disengage, and surf the side-lane resets between objectives.
edits.after: Before he ranks Riftwalk up his only escape is Flash — crash the wave and force the fight every time his 9s Null Sphere goes to farm.

edits.before: If Kassadin gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Riftwalk extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q resets and stay relevant through stacked windows.
edits.after: If Kassadin gets a kill he reaches the mana items that make Riftwalk spammable sooner — deny farm instead of dueling him, and shove waves so his blink keeps arriving to an empty lane.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry through the dance — Flawless Duet cancels his Null Sphere cast outright, and Vanguard's Edge walls the ground Riftwalk wants.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Kassadin's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, crash the wave into Kassadin: he cannot farm through your dives, and every level he misses delays the 2s Riftwalk.

edits.before: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 — hold four stacks so his blink back in lands into your stun, not into a fresh Irelia.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Null Sphere shields magic damage only, so your on-hit trade walks through it — and Flawless Duet cancels the cast outright.

edits.before: That is Kassadin’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Force Pulse cones 400 units and slows — never stand in it.

edits.before: Your dashes live in the wave's health bar — shoving mindlessly is deleting your own mobility.
edits.after: Mana items turn Riftwalk into spam — check whether he can afford three hops before you step.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Nether Blade is a 7s auto reset — the wind-up is the tell, so step back on the wind-up, not on the cast.

edits.before: Track Kassadin’s Riftwalk: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Kassadin’s Riftwalk: 5s at rank 1 down to 2s at rank 3 — until he ranks it up his only real exit is Flash.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Kassadin's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, crash the wave into Kassadin: he cannot farm through your dives, and every level he misses delays the 2s Riftwalk.

notes: FACT ERROR the user should know about: the content layer calls Null Sphere a silence in whys[0] ('short silence range'), early, and wants.foe[1]. Riot's current text gives Null Sphere damage, channel interruption and a magic-damage shield — no silence. I did not rewrite whys[0] because it is a level-chart row string and the fix belongs with a chart pass; wants.foe[1] and early would need the same correction across the champion. breakdown.wave and breakdown.early remain structurally templated — Kassadin offers no wave-specific hook I could ground without inventing.
